claims.claim: Crown Castle completed the $8.5B sale of its fiber and small-cell businesses on May 1, receiving about $8.4B before final adjustments and repositioning as a pure-play U.S. tower company with approximately 40,000 towers.

risks.risk: The divestiture reduces diversification and concentrates exposure in U.S. tower leasing and carrier capital cycles.

unknowns.unknown: Whether pure-play focus produces sustainably higher organic growth after customer churn remains unproven.

claims.claim: After closing the divestiture, Crown Castle allocated proceeds toward more than $7B of debt reduction and a $1B repurchase program; its July Q2 release updated full-year 2026 outlook with site-rental revenue midpoint of $3.855B.

risks.risk: Full-year site-rental revenue midpoint remains below 2025 actual, reflecting churn/cancellation pressure despite balance-sheet repair.

contradictions.contradiction: Balance-sheet simplification and debt reduction improve resilience while reported site-rental revenue outlook still implies contraction versus 2025.

unknowns.unknown: Post-sale normalized AFFO growth and reinvestment returns require full council underwriting.
